# How to Use This Book {.unnumbered}

The book follows the course of an audit. You first learn the language, then get the data ready, then look at it, test it, model it, and finally report. You do not have to read it all, or in order. Pick the way in that suits you.

:::: {.chapter-cards}
::: {.chapter-card}
[New to R](#sec-path-new)

Start from the beginning. No programming is assumed.
:::

::: {.chapter-card}
[Know some R already](#sec-path-know)

Skim the basics for the audit examples, and go to the tests.
:::

::: {.chapter-card}
[Have an audit question](audit-questions.qmd)

Look it up in the Audit Question Finder, and go straight to the answer.
:::
::::

## Path 1. New to R {#sec-path-new .unnumbered}

1. Read [Gearing Up](00-Zero.qmd). It shows how to install R and RStudio and run your first code.
2. Read Part I, *R Foundations*, in order. Its chapters build on one another.
3. Read Part II, *Getting Data Ready*. At the least, read @sec-read, @sec-clean, @sec-DPLYRR and @sec-joins. Almost every later chapter uses them.
4. Read Part IV, *Exploring and Sampling*, to learn to look at data before testing it.
5. After that, read the later parts in any order, as your audits need them.

## Path 2. Know some R already {#sec-path-know .unnumbered}

Skim Parts I and II for the newer features of R and the tidyverse, like the native pipe `|>`, and for their audit examples. Each chapter has an *Audit use case* section. Then go straight to Part V, *Forensic Tests*, or to whichever part your audit needs.

## Path 3. A short course for a first audit {#sec-path-short .unnumbered}

If you have about two weeks, these chapters will take you from nothing to a working set of audit tests.

1. [Gearing Up](00-Zero.qmd), @sec-basics, @sec-subset and @sec-pipes.
2. @sec-read, @sec-clean, @sec-DPLYRR and @sec-joins.
3. @sec-validate, @sec-dup and @sec-gaps.
4. @sec-reports, to put the results in front of the audit team.

## How the chapters are written {.unnumbered}

Most chapters follow the same plan, so that you always know where to look.

- **An audit problem** comes first, and the technique follows from it.
- **Data with planted cases.** Where real data cannot be shared, the chapter creates realistic data in R, and *plants* in it the irregularities to be found. These include a duplicate payment, a ghost employee and a tampered bank statement. The code that creates the data is folded away. Click on it to see it. Every number quoted in the text is computed from the data, so the text and the results always agree.
- **Callouts** mark what matters most for audit.

::: callout-tip
## Audit tip
Practical advice from audit experience.
:::

::: callout-caution
Traps to avoid, and points where the method can mislead.
:::

- **A suggested workflow** near the end of each chapter lists the steps to follow on your own data, and a **Remember** box sums up the main ideas.
- **A summary of functions used** closes each chapter, as a quick reference.

## Running the code {.unnumbered}

Every chunk of code in the book can be copied with the button at its top right. Function names in the code are links to their help pages. The packages needed for each part, with one command to install them all, are listed in @sec-packages. The datasets are described in @sec-datasets.
